Lesson — one verb, three times

Simple
tenses

Watch the verb. Only one small part changes each time.

PresentV1 (+s / es)
PastV2 / -ed
Futurewill + V1
Iwillplayed.

I play football every Saturday.

KruSlide ครูสไลด์© KruSlide01 / 03
Read "I play" together. Press → : "-ed" slides onto the verb and the marker moves to the past: "I played". Press → again: "will" drops in front, "-ed" falls off and the marker moves to the future: "I will play". Ask: what stays the same? (I, play). What changes? (-ed / will).
English grammarPractice · timelineM.1–3 · EP · 02

Where on the timeline?

Drag each sentence to its time — or tap it, then tap a time

He plays football every Saturday.
We watched a film yesterday.
They will take the test tomorrow.
She visited her grandma last weekend.
I will visit Chiang Mai next month.
My dad cooks dinner every evening.
KruSlide ครูสไลด์© KruSlide02 / 03
Students drag the six sentences above the timeline (or tap a sentence, then tap a time). Check marks each one. Press → to show the clue words in red: last weekend / yesterday = past; every Saturday / every evening = present (habit); tomorrow / next month (and will) = future.
English grammarPractice · writingM.1–3 · EP · 03

Fill the gaps.

Type the verb in the right tense — then press Check or Enter

01Last Sunday, Mai visit her grandparents.

02Yesterday it rain all day.

03Mai usually walk to school.

04Next year, she study at a new school.

Key

PastV2 / -edvisited · rained
PresentV1 + swalks (he / she / it)
Futurewill + V1will study

Students type each verb, then press Check (or Enter). Answers: visited, rained, walks, will study. The time words (Last Sunday, Yesterday, usually, next year) are the clues. Press → to show the key.
